label: GO step after a common a1->S1 trial that went unrewarded
explanation: Fires only at the GO step (D1/D2 essentially never), when the previous trial was a1 with a common transition to S1 and was unrewarded (a model-based switch-away-from-a1 situation). Uses only observed history. prev_reward==0 at GO alone covers 99.9% of mass but precision 0.18; adding previous choice a1 and common transition gives precision 0.93, recall 0.80 on dev. Essentially all misses are GO steps on the window first trial (rel -3) where the previous trial is outside the window (prev_action unknown), so the true recall is higher; it does not fire after rewarded trials, after a2 choices, or after rare a1->S2 trials. Firing is most reliable when the agent then still picks a1 (precision 0.99 with action==1), and the feature tends to be absent when the agent switches to a2, so it may relate to policy logit favouring a1 (choice in 2.8..8 bin); magnitude modulation not further checked.

issues: I reproduced the test scores exactly: P 0.919, R 0.801, F1 0.856, mass recall 0.84.
The phase claim holds. On dev, all 25838 GO activations account for 100% of activation mass. D1 has 5 activations and D2 has none.

The negative claims hold. a1 then rare to S2, unrewarded: P 0.002. a2 then rare, unrewarded: P 0.004. prev_reward==1: 1222 weak activations with about 0 mass. prev_action==2: 115 activations, mass 0.001.

Most misses are at rel -3, where prev_action and prev_common are unknown. rel -3 GO holds about 4167 of the roughly 5300 dev misses (~16% of mass). Restricting to rel > -3 gives P 0.93. This is a limit of the 5-trial window, not a flaw in the predicate. The other misses are scattered weak activations, mostly after rewarded trials.

The false positives follow a pattern: the predicate is true but the feature stays off when the agent goes on to switch to a2. Within the predicate, P is 0.99 if the next choice is a1 and 0.78 if it is a2. This is a graded drop, which the explanation already states, not a missing class. Adding action==1 lowers F1 to 0.75 because recall falls.

Choice-based alternatives score worse: prev unrewarded & choice a1, F1 0.43; with prev a1/unknown and logit > 2.8, F1 0.64. Using prev_state==1 instead of a1-common gives F1 0.54, so the feature tracks the a1-common pattern, not just reaching S1.
Minor: the weakest activation quartile has lower coverage (0.68), and magnitude was not studied. This does not undermine the label.
